learning_objective: 🎯 Explore precision, reflexes, and discipline through racket sports (Badminton, Table Tennis) and combat sports (Judo, Taekwondo)!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A racket sport played with a shuttlecock. It requires excellent agility, wrist flexibility, and quick reflexes. A match is usually best of 3 games of 21 points each.
Also known as ping-pong. Played on a hard table divided by a net. It is the fastest racket sport in the world, requiring intense focus and spin control.
Judo focuses on grappling, throws, and pinning the opponent. Taekwondo heavily emphasizes fast, high, and spinning kicks. Both teach extreme mental discipline and self-defense.
Knowing the exact dimensions of a badminton court (13.4m x 6.1m for doubles) or a TT table (2.74m long) is essential for standard play.
Individual sports require reading the opponent's weaknesses, managing your own stamina, and constantly adjusting your game plan without the help of teammates.

fun_activity.title: 🏸 Book and Lemon Balance
fun_activity.instructions: Don't have a racket? Take a hardbound book and a lemon (or small ball). Try to bounce the lemon on the book as many times as you can without letting it fall. It builds hand-eye coordination!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the scoring system of Badminton (rally point system up to 21).
📌 Know the fundamental skills of Table Tennis (Serve, Drive, Push, Smash).
quick_recap: ⭐ In badminton, if the score becomes 20-all, the side which gains a 2-point lead first wins.
⭐ Table Tennis requires players to serve diagonally only during doubles play.
⭐ Martial arts emphasize respect; players always bow to each other before and after a match.
